column3: The outbox pattern is a way to safely and reliably exchange data between multiple (micro) services (`debezium-outbox-event-router#dbz-doc-main`).
column5: The outbox pattern is a way to safely and reliably exchange data between multiple (micro) services.

column3: To implement the outbox pattern in a Debezium application, a connector is configured to capture changes in an outbox table and to apply the Debezium outbox event router single message transformation (`debezium-outbox-event-router#dbz-doc-main`).
column5: To implement the outbox pattern in a Debezium application, configure a Debezium connector to: Capture changes in an outbox table Apply the Debezium outbox event router single message transformation (SMT)

column3: A connector can capture changes in more than one outbox table only if each outbox table has the same structure (`debezium-outbox-event-router#dbz-doc-main`).
column5: A connector can capture changes in more than one outbox table only if each outbox table has the same structure.

column3: The outbox event router SMT is not compatible with the MongoDB connector (`debezium-outbox-event-router#dbz-doc-main`).
column5: The outbox event router SMT is not compatible with the MongoDB connector.

column3: To configure a Debezium connector to support the outbox pattern, the `outbox.EventRouter` SMT is configured (`debezium-outbox-event-router#basic-outbox-configuration`).
column5: To configure a Debezium connector to support the outbox pattern, configure the outbox.EventRouter SMT.

column3: The default outbox table has the columns `id`, `aggregatetype`, `aggregateid`, `type` and `payload` (`debezium-outbox-event-router#basic-outbox-table`).
column5: id | uuid | not null aggregatetype | character varying(255) | not null aggregateid | character varying(255) | not null type | character varying(255) | not null payload | jsonb |

column3: `id` | Contains the unique ID of the event, which is a header in an outbox message and can be used to remove duplicate messages.
column5: Contains the unique ID of the event. In an outbox message, this value is a header. You can use this ID, for example, to remove duplicate messages.

column3: `aggregatetype` | Contains a value that the SMT appends to the name of the topic to which the connector emits an outbox message.
column5: Contains a value that the SMT appends to the name of the topic to which the connector emits an outbox message.

column3: `aggregateid` | Contains the event key, which the SMT uses as the key in the emitted outbox message.
column5: Contains the event key, which provides an ID for the payload. The SMT uses this value as the key in the emitted outbox message.

column3: `payload` | A representation of the outbox change event, in JSON by default.
column5: A representation of the outbox change event. The default structure is JSON.

column3: The `aggregateid` value as the message key is important for maintaining correct order in Kafka partitions (`debezium-outbox-event-router#basic-outbox-table`).
column5: This is important for maintaining correct order in Kafka partitions.

column3: By default, the Kafka message value is solely comprised of the payload value (`debezium-outbox-event-router#basic-outbox-table`).
column5: By default, the Kafka message value is solely comprised of the payload value.

column3: In a default configuration, `route.by.field` is set to `aggregatetype` and `route.topic.replacement` is set to `outbox.event.${routedByValue}` (`debezium-outbox-event-router#basic-outbox-table`).
column5: the route.by.field SMT option is set to aggregatetype and the route.topic.replacement SMT option is set to outbox.event.${routedByValue}.

column3: With `SKIP LOCKED`, any selected rows that cannot be immediately locked are skipped (`pg-sql-select#SQL-FOR-UPDATE-SHARE`).

column3: To prevent an operation from waiting for other transactions to commit, `NOWAIT` or `SKIP LOCKED` is used (`pg-sql-select#SQL-FOR-UPDATE-SHARE`).
column5: To prevent the operation from waiting for other transactions to commit, use either the NOWAIT or SKIP LOCKED option.

column3: With `NOWAIT`, the statement reports an error, rather than waiting, if a selected row cannot be locked immediately (`pg-sql-select#SQL-FOR-UPDATE-SHARE`).
column5: With NOWAIT, the statement reports an error, rather than waiting, if a selected row cannot be locked immediately.

column3: Skipping locked rows provides an inconsistent view of the data, so it is not suitable for general purpose work (`pg-sql-select#SQL-FOR-UPDATE-SHARE`).

column3: Skipping locked rows can be used to avoid lock contention with multiple consumers accessing a queue-like table (`pg-sql-select#SQL-FOR-UPDATE-SHARE`).

column3: `FOR UPDATE` prevents the rows from being locked, modified or deleted by other transactions until the current transaction ends (`pg-explicit-locking#LOCKING-ROWS`).
column5: This prevents them from being locked, modified or deleted by other transactions until the current transaction ends.

column3: Row-level locks are released at transaction end or during savepoint rollback (`pg-explicit-locking#LOCKING-ROWS`).
column5: Row-level locks are released at transaction end or during savepoint rollback, just like table-level locks.

column3: PostgreSQL's logical decoding allows the extraction of the changes that were committed to the transaction log and their processing with the help of an output plug-in (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-overview`).
column5: It is a mechanism that allows the extraction of the changes that were committed to the transaction log and the processing of these changes in a user-friendly manner with the help of an output plug-in.

column3: `pgoutput` is the standard logical decoding output plug-in in PostgreSQL 10+ (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-overview`).
column5: The standard logical decoding output plug-in in PostgreSQL 10+.

column3: `decoderbufs` is a decoding plug-in based on Protobuf and maintained by the Debezium community (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-overview`).
column5: Decoding plug-in that is based on Protobuf and maintained by the Debezium community.

column3: The PostgreSQL connector produces a change event for every row-level insert, update and delete operation that was captured, and sends the records for each table to a separate Kafka topic (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-overview`).
column5: The connector produces a change event for every row-level insert, update, and delete operation that was captured and sends change event records for each table in a separate Kafka topic.

column3: When it first connects to a database, the PostgreSQL connector performs a consistent snapshot of each of the database schemas (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-overview`).
column5: Therefore, when the PostgreSQL connector first connects to a particular PostgreSQL database, it starts by performing a consistent snapshot of each of the database schemas.

column3: PostgreSQL normally purges write-ahead log segments after some period of time (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-overview`).
column5: PostgreSQL normally purges write-ahead log (WAL) segments after some period of time.

column3: The connector records the WAL position for each event (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-overview`).
column5: As the connector reads changes and produces events, it records the WAL position for each event.

column3: If the connector stops for any reason, upon restart it continues reading the WAL where it last left off (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-overview`).
column5: upon restart the connector continues reading the WAL where it last left off.

column3: If the connector stops during a snapshot, it begins a new snapshot when it restarts (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-overview`).
column5: If the connector stops during a snapshot, the connector begins a new snapshot when it restarts.

column3: Logical decoding does not support DDL changes (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-overview`).
column5: Logical decoding does not support DDL changes.

column3: The Kafka Connect process asynchronously writes the change event records in the same order in which they were generated to the appropriate Kafka topic (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-streaming-changes`).
column5: The Kafka Connect process asynchronously writes the change event records in the same order in which they were generated to the appropriate Kafka topic.

column3: For the PostgreSQL connector, the LSN recorded in each change event is the offset (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-streaming-changes`).
column5: For the PostgreSQL connector, the LSN recorded in each change event is the offset.

column3: When the connector restarts, it asks the PostgreSQL server to send the events starting just after the last recorded position (`debezium-postgresql#postgresql-streaming-changes`).
column5: When the connector restarts, it sends a request to the PostgreSQL server to send the events starting just after that position.

column3: A retry can repeat an external call, so a stable idempotency key is used when that call must tolerate repetition (`axon-migration-sagas-to-workflows#sagas-and-workflows`).

column3: The consequence of token stealing in an Axon streaming event processor is that an event may be handled twice, or more (`axon-event-processors-streaming#_what_are_the_consequences_of_token_stealing`).
column5: The consequence of token stealing is that an event may be handled twice (or more).

column3: When an event handling task cannot be rolled back nor performed in an idempotent fashion, compensating actions are the way out (`axon-event-processors-streaming#_what_are_the_consequences_of_token_stealing`).
column5: When the task cannot be rolled back nor performed in an idempotent fashion, compensating actions are the way out.

column3: If a rollback is out of the question for an event handling task, Axon strongly recommends making the task idempotent (`axon-event-processors-streaming#_what_are_the_consequences_of_token_stealing`).
column5: If a rollback is out of the question for an event handling task, we strongly recommend making the task idempotent.
